body:
Ran the exemplar parity tier end to end. It passes, and it is the most valuable artefact in this repository for adoption.

  02  rdm() over 577 centres                              1.07 s
      self-verification vs a direct loop at 8 centres     max abs diff 3.33e-16
      rsa() over 577 centres                              1.91 s
  03  crossnobis folds verified as per-run means          max abs diff 0
      rMVPA native crossnobis RDM, 577 centres            0.50 s
  04  both arms: 577 centres, identical ids and sphere sizes, radius 11.25 mm

      MATCHED ESTIMAND, cross-validated squared Euclidean RDM
        entries compared        16156   (577 centres x 28 pairs)
        max abs difference      1.33e-15
        centres above tolerance 0 / 577
        GATE (<= 1e-08)         PASS
      SHARED SPEARMAN SCORE     max abs difference 0e+00

Two independent implementations, different codebases, same real data, agreeing at 1.33e-15 over sixteen thousand entries, with derived scores agreeing to exactly zero. That is an identity claim rather than a similarity claim, and anyone can check it in twenty seconds.

NOTHING IN MY REVIEW SUGGESTED BUILDING THIS. Five of my beads asked for a worked example on real data; none asked for a head-to-head against the incumbent with a numerical gate. It answers the question every prospective adopter actually asks - does this give the same answer as the tool I already trust - and my review did not think to ask it.

It is also the counter-instance to the thesis I spent the day arguing. I claimed the documentation systematically undersells the package. Here is the strongest possible statement of what the package does, made numerically, already in the repository - and reachable only by someone who cloned it and went looking in a subdirectory. Filed bd- for surfacing it in the README and pkgdown landing page.

TWO HONEST NOTES. The README's cost claim for THIS tier is accurate - about 20 s, and it runs in seconds - which contrasts with the error-channel arm's cost claim being tenfold stale. The exemplar docs are not uniformly wrong about cost; one section is right and one is not.

And on speed the incumbent wins this operation: rMVPA 0.50 s against effectagram 1.07 s for the same RDM, about 2x. Worth stating plainly in a document whose purpose is honest comparison. effectagram's argument is not speed - it is that the same number falls out of a general evidence form that also yields contrast, RSA, coupling and calibrated uncertainty from one object, none of which the incumbent provides.

Method note: this is execution-based verification, and today that category has held without exception while every one of my six performance claims failed. I am going to stay in it.
